headline: Q1: Streaming + Auth hardening land in parallel; Q2 brings tool-calling pipeline overhaul
body:
Two Q1 workstreams (both effort 8, no cross-dependencies) target foundational reliability gaps, followed by a Q2 tool-calling hardening effort.

Streaming: fixes span provider SSE parsing (tolerate proxies, e.g. Anthropic-via-Bedrock, that omit the 'event:' field instead of hard-failing with zero generation chunks), structured-output streaming (stop spurious Pydantic serializer warnings and stop silently dropping response metadata/headers like x-request-id), disable_streaming='tool_calling' (currently crashes with an AttributeError because an AsyncStream object is passed where a ChatCompletion is expected — and even when it doesn't crash, it disables streaming globally instead of scoping to tool-calling turns), and agent/graph execution paths that internally call ainvoke instead of astream, meaning on_llm_new_token never fires even when graph-level streaming is enabled. There's also a known-incorrect assertion in the core streaming error-callback test suite masking whether error-path behavior is actually correct, plus gaps in standard test coverage/release sequencing for tool-call streaming across integration packages (including unreleased ones like Mistral). Flag if you're touching SSE parsing or the astream/ainvoke routing — both carry regression risk (masking malformed responses, or performance/ordering changes in frameworks not built for token-level streaming).

Authentication: ChatAnthropic (and similar integrations) need custom HTTP client support with mTLS for corporate proxy/PKI setups. MCP tool discovery is dropping auth headers/tokens during discovery, causing spurious 403s despite correct credentials. AzureChatOpenAI and BaseChatOpenAI don't share httpx client/connection-pooling setup, causing redundant connections and inconsistent behavior — the plan is a shared layer across providers, starting with at least two migrated integrations. Separately, SSRF/allowlist host validation can be bypassed via environment-based auth checks; this is flagged high-risk since hardening it could break legitimate enterprise configs that currently rely on env-based auth to reach internal hosts — worth weighing in on scoping before it ships.

Q2 tool-calling work (dependent on nothing, but sequenced after Q1) covers: Gemini's strict turn-order/thought-signature validation rejecting injected tool-call history; malformed/fragmented streamed tool-call payloads crashing or silently executing the wrong tool; agents forcing tool_choice='required' breaking reasoning models that only support 'auto'/'none'; ToolNode executing tool calls a human has rejected (safety-critical HITL gap); tool_call_id missing from on_tool_start/on_tool_end making parallel tool-call attribution impossible; tool-call limits enforced only after the fact with no proactive warning; and inconsistent handle_tool_error/ToolException behavior between @tool, ToolNode, and wrap_tool_call middleware.
call_to_action: Review the SSRF/allowlist hardening scope and the astream-routing change in the streaming PRD for regression risk before Q1 work is sequenced — both touch existing behavior that some users may currently depend on.
